entries.answer: A player is offside if, at the moment the ball is played to them, they are nearer the opponent's goal line than both the ball and the second-last defender. The rule exists to stop a single long pass producing an easy chance. What makes it confusing is that being offside is judged at the pass, not at the shot, so a player can run twenty yards after a through ball and still be flagged for where they were when it was played.

entries.answer: A penalty is awarded for a foul inside the penalty area, and the kick is taken from a fixed spot twelve yards from the goal with only the goalkeeper allowed to move. The apparent unfairness is deliberate: it is the only position on the pitch where a goal is scored more often than not, because the dive narrows the angle. The rule that decides most penalties is the one about which foot or body part made contact, not how hard.

patterns: when do you get a corner
entries.answer: A corner is awarded when the defending team puts the ball over their own goal line, last touched by an attacker. It is taken from the corner of the pitch nearest the goal, which is why attacking set pieces are aimed short. The expected goal value of a corner is low, and a corner won from a good cross is usually worth more than the one from a long delivery everyone can head.

patterns: how strict is the handball rule
entries.answer: Handball is a deliberate or reckless contact with the ball by the arm or hand, and the offence is called handball rather than a foul, which reflects how strictly it is policed. The rule is about the position of the arm rather than the intent, because a player cannot always tell a bounce off a defender's chest from one off their arm. A handball inside the area is a penalty, and a handball anywhere while scoring is a red card.

entries.answer: A substitution swaps one player for another during play, and most competitions allow a set number rather than a rolling stream. The limit is a tactical tool as much as a physical one: three substitutions means a manager who has used them has committed to the shape on the pitch. Historically the limit was one, and the move to five was about player welfare and about broadcasters.

patterns: how often is the world cup
who has won the most world cups
entries.answer: The FIFA World Cup is held every four years and is the oldest international football competition, first staged in 1930. Brazil is the only nation to have won it five times, and no team has won it on home soil except two. The tournament expanded from 24 to 32 teams in 1998, which lengthened it and diluted the group stage without making the knockout rounds any easier.
